39| 40|

41| 42|

43| 44| ## Introduction 45| 46| **UniAR** is a unified autoregressive multimodal model that handles **image understanding**, **image generation**, and **image editing** in a single Transformer. Unlike prior unified models that rely on two separate visual tokenizers (splitting the representation space), UniAR uses a **single discrete visual tokenizer** as the key bridge between understanding and generation, enabling a **shared context** in which the model can directly interpret its own generated visual tokens without additional re-encoding. 47| 48| Key design choices: 49| - **Multi-level BSQ tokenizer** — fuses shallow (low-level detail) and deep (high-level semantic) visual features via lookup-free Binary Spherical Quantization, scaling the effective vocabulary to 264 codes with minimal overhead. 50| - **Parallel bitwise prediction** — jointly predicts spatially grouped, multi-level visual codes per AR step, achieving a **32x visual compression ratio** (a 1024x1024 image needs only 256 AR tokens). 51| - **DiT-based visual decoder** — an SD3-medium transformer with semantic visual feature injection that reconstructs high-fidelity images from discrete visual tokens, with resolution upsampling support. 52| 53| 54| ## News 55| - **[2026/07]** We provide an online demo for UniAR. Feel free to try it online. Thanks to @apolinario for the implementation. [![🚀 Hugging Face Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%9A%80%20Hugging%20Face-Demo-FFCC4D.svg)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ShareLab-SII/uniar) 56| - **[2026/06]** Code and model weights released. 57| - **[2026/05]** UniAR is accepted by ICML 2026 🎉 ! 58| 59| ## TODO 60| 61| - [ ] Release visual decoder training code. 62| 63| ## Getting Started 64| 65| ### Installation 66| 67| ```bash 68| conda create -n uniar python=3.12 -y 69| conda activate uniar 70| 71| git clone https://github.com/ShareLab-SII/UniAR.git 72| cd UniAR 73| pip install -e . # inference dependencies 74| pip install -e ".[train]" # additional training dependencies (deepspeed, datasets, etc.) 75| pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation # highly recommended for faster attention 76| ``` 77| 78| Requirements: Python 3.12, CUDA 12.1+, GPU with >= 24 GB VRAM for inference. 79| 80| ### Checkpoints 81| 82| Download the UniAR checkpoint (contains AR model + visual decoder components): 83| 84| | Component | Role | 85| |-----------|------| 86| | `ar_model` | Unified autoregressive model | 87| | `bsq_encoder` | BSQ quantized image tokenizer | 88| | `sd3_transformer` | SD3 transformer with visual feature injection | 89| | `sd3_pipeline` | SD3 pipeline (VAE + text encoders) | 90| 91| ```bash 92| huggingface-cli download https://huggingface.co/ShareLab-SII/UniAR-RL --local-dir checkpoints/UniAR-RL 93| huggingface-cli download https://huggingface.co/ShareLab-SII/UniAR-SFT --local-dir checkpoints/UniAR-SFT 94| ``` 95| 96| ## Inference 97| 98| ### Image Understanding 99| 100| ```bash 101| conda activate uniar 102| python inference/chat.py \ 103| --model_path checkpoints/UniAR-RL \ 104| --image https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-VL/assets/demo.jpeg \ 105| --prompt "Describe this image in detail." 106| ``` 107| 108| ### Image Generation 109| 110| ```bash 111| conda activate uniar 112| python inference/generate.py \ 113| --model_path checkpoints/UniAR-RL \ 114| --prompt "A cute anime girl." \ 115| --output_path output.png 116| ``` 117| 118| See [docs/inference.md](docs/inference.md) for the full parameter reference and advanced usage. 119| 120| ### Online Demo [![🚀 Hugging Face Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%9A%80%20Hugging%20Face-Demo-FFCC4D.svg)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ShareLab-SII/uniar) 121| You can also try UniAR via our [online demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ShareLab-SII/uniar). 122| 123| ## Evaluation 124| 125| We provide a unified batch inference script ([`inference/generate_batch.py`](inference/generate_batch.py)) that supports **multi-node, multi-GPU** distributed generation via `accelerate`. All outputs are organized in a standard directory structure: 126| 127| ``` 128| // 129| ├── 00000/ 130| │ ├── metadata.json 131| │ └── samples/ 132| │ ├── 0000.png 133| │ ├── 0001.png 134| │ └── ... 135| ├── 00001/ 136| │ └── ... 137| ``` 138| 139| To evaluate on specific benchmarks, we provide conversion scripts under [`eval/convert_structure/`](eval/convert_structure/) that transform our unified output layout into each benchmark's expected format. 140| 141| See [docs/evaluation.md](docs/evaluation.md) for the full evaluation guide. 142| 143| ## Training 144| 145| ### Reinforcement Learning 146| 147| UniAR uses GRPO with a multi-reward stack for reinforcement learning on image generation. The training system runs across multiple nodes: decode servers (BSQ visual codes → images), reward servers (scoring), and training nodes (AR rollout + GRPO updates). 148| 149| See [docs/training_rl.md](docs/training_rl.md) for the complete setup guide. 150| 151| ## Acknowledgements 152| 153| UniAR builds upon several excellent open-source projects: 154| 155| - [Qwen3-VL](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL) 156| - [X-Omni](https://github.com/X-Omni-Team/X-Omni) 157| - [DeepStack](https://github.com/MengLcool/DeepStack-VL) 158| - [Infinity](https://github.com/FoundationVision/Infinity) 159| - [Stable Diffusion 3](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-diffusion-3.5-medium) 160| - [TRL](https://github.com/huggingface/trl) 161| 162| We also thank the benchmark authors for their evaluation tools: 163| [GenEval](https://github.com/djghosh13/geneval), 164| [OneIG-Bench](https://github.com/OneIG-Bench/OneIG-Benchmark), 165| [LongText-Bench](https://github.com/X-Omni-Team/X-Omni), 166| [ImgEdit](https://github.com/PKU-YuanGroup/ImgEdit). 167| 168| ## Citation 169| 170| If you find UniAR useful in your research, please consider citing: 171| 172| ```bibtex 173| @article{peng2026unified, 174| title={Unified Multimodal Autoregressive Modeling with Shared Context-Visual Tokenizer is Key to Unification}, 175| author={Peng, Wujian and Meng, Lingchen and Cai, Yuxuan and Zhuang, Xianwei and Yang, Yuhuan and Fang, Rongyao and Wu, Chenfei and Lin, Junyang and Wu, Zuxuan and Bai, Shuai}, 176| journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.18249}, 177| year={2026} 178| } 179| ``` (End of file — 179 lines total)

1| # [ICML 2026] Autoregressive Image Generation with Masked Bit Modeling 2| 3|
4| 5| [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Website-87CEEB)](https://bar-gen.github.io/)   6| [![paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-Paper-.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09024)   7| 8|
9| 10| ## Introduction 11| 12| Visual generative models have driven remarkable progress across computer vision tasks. A central component of these systems is **visual tokenization**, which compresses high-dimensional pixel inputs into compact latent representations. Depending on quantization strategies, visual tokenization pipelines can be categorized into *discrete* and *continuous* approaches. While continuous tokenizers with diffusion models currently dominate visual generation, we investigate whether this gap is fundamental or merely a consequence of design choices. 13| 14| We introduce **BAR** (*masked **B**it **A**uto**R**egressive modeling*), a strong discrete visual generation framework that challenges the prevailing dominance of continuous pipelines. Our key insight is that the commonly observed inferior performance of discrete tokenizers is largely attributable to their substantially higher compression ratios, which lead to severe information loss. 15| 16| ### Key Findings 17| 18| **1. Discrete Tokenizers Beat Continuous Tokenizers** 19| By scaling the codebook size to match the bit budget of continuous tokenizers, we demonstrate that discrete tokenizers can achieve competitive or superior reconstruction quality. 20| 21| **2. Discrete Autoregressive Models Beat Diffusion** 22| We address the vocabulary scaling problem by replacing the standard linear prediction head with a lightweight **Masked Bit Modeling (MBM)** head. This design enables training with arbitrary codebook sizes while maintaining superior generation quality. BAR achieves state-of-the-art gFID of **0.99** on ImageNet-256, surpassing leading continuous and discrete approaches. 23| 24| **3. Superior Efficiency** 25| BAR offers reduced sampling costs and faster convergence compared to diffusion models. Our efficient variant BAR-B/4 achieves 2.94× speedup over MeanFlow while matching its performance, and BAR-B is 3.68× faster than RAE while achieving same FID (1.13 vs 1.13). 26| 27|

28| 29|

30|

31| By measuring information capacity in bits, we enable direct comparison between discrete and continuous tokenizers. Our discrete tokenizer (BAR-FSQ) scales smoothly with codebook size and matches or surpasses continuous tokenizers at sufficient bit budgets. 32|

33| 34|

35| 36|

37|

38| BAR establishes a new state of the art across both discrete and continuous paradigms. With only 415M parameters, BAR-B achieves gFID of 1.13, matching RAE while being significantly faster. BAR-L (1.1B parameters) achieves a record gFID of 0.99. 39|

40| 41| ## Method Overview 42| 43| ### BAR Framework 44| 45| BAR decomposes autoregressive visual generation into two stages: 46| 47| 1. **Context Modeling**: An autoregressive transformer captures global structure via causal attention, generating latent conditions for each token position. 48| 49| 2. **Token Prediction**: Instead of a standard linear head that scales poorly with large vocabularies, we introduce a **Masked Bit Modeling (MBM)** head that generates discrete tokens through progressive bit-wise unmasking. 50| 51| ### Masked Bit Modeling Head 52| 53| The MBM head treats token prediction as a conditional generation task rather than massive classification: 54| - **Scalability**: Memory complexity reduces from O(C) to O(log₂ C), where C is codebook size 55| - **Quality**: Bit-wise masking acts as a strong regularizer, consistently improving generation quality 56| - **Flexibility**: Supports arbitrary codebook sizes without architectural changes 57| 58| At inference, the MBM head generates each token via iterative unmasking with a configurable schedule (e.g., [2, 2, 5, 7] unmasks 2, 2, 5, then 7 bits across 4 steps). 59| 60| ## Model Zoo 61| 62| We provide pretrained generator models: 63| 64| | Model | Config | Size | gFID | IS | 65| | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | 66| | BAR-B/4 | [bar_b_patch4.yaml](configs/generator/bar_b_patch4.yaml) | 416M | 2.34 | 274.7 | 67| | BAR-B/2 | [bar_b_patch2.yaml](configs/generator/bar_b_patch2.yaml) | 415M | 1.35 | 293.4 | 68| | BAR-B | [bar_b.yaml](configs/generator/bar_b.yaml) | 415M | 1.13 | 289.0 | 69| | BAR-L | [bar_l.yaml](configs/generator/bar_l.yaml) | 1.1B | 0.99 | 296.9 | 70| | BAR-L-res512 | [bar_l_res512.yaml](configs/generator/bar_l_res512.yaml) | 1.1B | 1.09 | 311.1 | 71| 72| 73| ## Preparation 74| 75| ### Environment Setup 76| ```shell 77| pip3 install -r requirements.txt 78| ``` 79| 80| ### Checkpoint Setup 81| 82| **Download Model Checkpoints from HuggingFace:** 83| ```bash 84| pip install huggingface_hub 85| hf download FAR-Amazon/BAR-collections \ 86| --local-dir assets 87| ``` 88| 89| This will download all pretrained models (generators, tokenizers, and discriminator weights) to the `assets/` folder. 90| 91| ## Quick Start 92| 93| ### Training 94| 95| **Data Preparation:** 96| 97| We use webdataset format for data loading. To begin with, it is needed to convert the dataset into webdataset format. An example script to convert ImageNet to wds format is provided [here](https://github.com/bytedance/1d-tokenizer/blob/main/data/convert_imagenet_to_wds.py). 98| 99| **Train BAR-FSQ Tokenizer:** 100| ```bash 101| WANDB_MODE=offline WORKSPACE=/path/to/workspace \ 102| accelerate launch --num_machines=1 --num_processes=8 \ 103| --machine_rank=0 --main_process_ip=127.0.0.1 \ 104| --main_process_port=9999 --same_network \ 105| scripts/train_bar_fsq.py \ 106| config=configs/tokenizer/bar_fsq_16bits.yaml \ 107| dataset.params.train_shards_path_or_url=/path/to/imagenet-train-{000000..000320}.tar \ 108| dataset.params.eval_shards_path_or_url=/path/to/imagenet-val-{000000..000049}.tar 109| ``` 110| 111| **Train BAR Generator:** 112| 113| Optionally pretokenize ImageNet dataset to NPZ format for faster training: 114| ```bash 115| # Note: data_path should point to ImageNet in original jpeg format (train/ and val/ folders) 116| torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 scripts/pretokenization.py \ 117| --img_size 256 \ 118| --batch_size 32 \ 119| --vae_config_path configs/tokenizer/bar_fsq_16bits.yaml \ 120| --vae_path assets/tokenizer/bar_fsq_16bits.bin \ 121| --data_path /path/to/imagenet \ 122| --cached_path ./pretokenized_npz 123| ``` 124| 125| Train the generator: 126| 127| With pretokenization: 128| ```bash 129| WANDB_MODE=offline WORKSPACE=/path/to/workspace \ 130| accelerate launch --num_machines=N --num_processes=$((8*N)) \ 131| --machine_rank=RANK --main_process_ip=MAIN_IP \ 132| --main_process_port=9999 --same_network \ 133| scripts/train_bar.py \ 134| config=configs/generator/bar_b_patch4.yaml \ 135| dataset.params.pretokenization=./pretokenized_npz \ 136| training.per_gpu_batch_size=$((2048 / (8*N))) 137| ``` 138| 139| Without pretokenization: 140| ```bash 141| WANDB_MODE=offline WORKSPACE=/path/to/workspace \ 142| accelerate launch --num_machines=N --num_processes=$((8*N)) \ 143| --machine_rank=RANK --main_process_ip=MAIN_IP \ 144| --main_process_port=9999 --same_network \ 145| scripts/train_bar.py \ 146| config=configs/generator/bar_b_patch4.yaml \ 147| dataset.params.train_shards_path_or_url=/path/to/imagenet-train-{000000..000320}.tar \ 148| dataset.params.eval_shards_path_or_url=/path/to/imagenet-val-{000000..000049}.tar \ 149| training.per_gpu_batch_size=$((2048 / (8*N))) 150| ``` 151| 152| ## Evaluation on ImageNet-1K 153| 154| We provide a [sampling script](./sample_imagenet.py) for reproducing generation results on ImageNet-1K benchmark. 155| 156| ### Setup Evaluation Tools 157| ```bash 158| # Prepare ADM evaluation script 159| git clone https://github.com/openai/guided-diffusion.git 160| 161| # Download reference statistics 162| wget https://openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net/diffusion/jul-2021/ref_batches/imagenet/256/VIRTUAL_imagenet256_labeled.npz 163| ``` 164| 165| ### Generate and Evaluate 166| 167| **Example: BAR-B/4** 168| ```bash 169| # Generate samples 170| torchrun --nnodes=1 --nproc_per_node=1 --rdzv-endpoint=localhost:9999 \ 171| sample_imagenet.py \ 172| config=configs/generator/bar_b_patch4.yaml \ 173| experiment.output_dir="bar_b_patch4" \ 174| experiment.generator_checkpoint=assets/generator/bar_b_patch4.bin \ 175| experiment.tokenizer_checkpoint=assets/tokenizer/bar_fsq_16bits.bin \ 176| model.generator.guidance_scale=9.6 \ 177| model.generator.mbm_head.randomize_temperature=1.4 \ 178| 'model.generator.mbm_head.tokens_allocation=[64,64,64,64]' 179| 180| # 8| 9| > Autoregressive models—generating content step-by-step like reading a sentence—excel in language but struggle with images. 6| import torch
7| import torch.nn as nn
8| from torch.autograd import Function
9| 
10| 
11| CODE_USAGE = set()
12| _BSQ_LOSS = []
13| 
14| 
15| def save_bsq_loss(routing_results):
16|     global _BSQ_LOSS
17|     _BSQ_LOSS.append(routing_results)
18| 
19| 
20| def get_bsq_loss():

22|     return _BSQ_LOSS
23|

30| class DifferentiableEntropyFunction(Function):
31|     @staticmethod
32|     def forward(ctx, zq, basis, K, eps):
33|         zb = (zq + 1) / 2
34|         zi = ((zb * basis).sum(-1)).to(torch.int64)
35|         cnt = torch.scatter_reduce(
36|             torch.zeros(2**K, device=zq.device, dtype=zq.dtype),
37|             0,
38|             zi.flatten(),
39|             torch.ones_like(zi.flatten()).to(zq.dtype),
40|             'sum'
41|         )
42|         prob = (cnt + eps) / (cnt + eps).sum()
43|         H = -(prob * torch.log(prob)).sum()
44|         ctx.save_for_backward(zq, zi, prob)
45|         ctx.K = K
46|         return H
47| 
48|     @staticmethod
49|     def backward(ctx, grad_output):
50|         zq, zi, prob = ctx.saved_tensors
51|         grad_array = -grad_output * (torch.log(prob) + 1) / zi.numel() / ctx.K
52|         reord_grad = grad_array[zi.flatten()].reshape(zi.shape)
53|         grad_input = reord_grad.unsqueeze(-1) * zq
54|         return grad_input, None, None, None, None
55| 
56| 
57| def codebook_entropy(zq, basis, K, eps=1e-4):
58|     return DifferentiableEntropyFunction.apply(zq, basis, K, eps)

61| class BinarySphericalQuantizer(nn.Module):
62|     def __init__(
63|         self,
64|         embed_dim,
65|         beta=0,
66|         gamma0=1,
67|         gamma=1,
68|         zeta=1,
69|         input_format='bchw',
70|         soft_entropy=True,
71|         group_size=1,
72|         persample_entropy_compute='analytical',
73|         cb_entropy_compute='group',
74|         l2_norm=True,
75|         inv_temperature=1,
76|     ):
77|         super().__init__()
78|         self.embed_dim = embed_dim
79|         self.beta = beta
80|         self.gamma0 = gamma0
81|         self.gamma = gamma
82|         self.zeta = zeta
83|         self.input_format = input_format
84|         assert self.embed_dim % group_size == 0, "embed_dim must be divisible by group_size"
85|         self.num_groups = self.embed_dim // group_size
86|         self.group_size = group_size
87|         assert persample_entropy_compute in ['group', 'analytical'], \
88|             "persample_entropy_compute must be either 'group' or 'analytical'"
89|         assert cb_entropy_compute in ['group', 'nce'], \
90|             "cb_entropy_compute must be either 'group' or 'nce'"
91|         self.persample_entropy_compute = persample_entropy_compute
92|         self.cb_entropy_compute = cb_entropy_compute
93|         self.l2_norm = l2_norm
94|         self.inv_temperature = inv_temperature
95| 
96|         self.register_buffer('basis', 2 ** torch.arange(embed_dim - 1, -1, -1))
97|         self.register_buffer('group_basis', 2 ** torch.arange(group_size - 1, -1, -1))
98| 
99|         self.num_dimensions = 2 ** embed_dim
100|         self.bits_per_index = embed_dim
101| 
102|         group_codes = torch.arange(2 ** self.group_size)
103|         group_codebook = self.indexes_to_codes(group_codes).float()[:, -group_size:]
104|         self.register_buffer('group_codebook', group_codebook, persistent=False)
105| 
106|         self.soft_entropy = soft_entropy
107| 
108|     def quantize(self, z):
109|         assert z.shape[-1] == self.embed_dim, f"Expected {self.embed_dim} dimensions, got {z.shape[-1]}"
110|         zhat = torch.where(
111|             z > 0,
112|             torch.tensor(1, dtype=z.dtype, device=z.device),
113|             torch.tensor(-1, dtype=z.dtype, device=z.device),
114|         )
115|         return z + (zhat - z).detach()

119|             z = rearrange(z, 'b c h w -> b h w c')

124|         if not self.training:

131|         if self.soft_entropy:
132|             persample_entropy, cb_entropy, avg_prob = self.soft_entropy_loss(z)
133|             entropy_penalty = self.gamma0 * persample_entropy - self.gamma * cb_entropy

137|             cb_entropy = codebook_entropy(zq, self.basis, self.embed_dim)
138|             entropy_penalty = self.gamma0 * persample_entropy - self.gamma * cb_entropy
139| 
140|         commit_loss = self.beta * torch.mean(((zq.detach() - z) ** 2).sum(dim=-1))
141| 
142|         zq = zq * q_scale
143|         if used_codes is not None:
144|             for x in used_codes.tolist():
145|                 CODE_USAGE.add(x)
146| 
147|         if self.input_format == 'bchw':
148|             zq = rearrange(zq, 'b h w c -> b c h w')
149| 
150|         return (
151|             zq,
152|             commit_loss + self.zeta * entropy_penalty / self.inv_temperature,
153|             {
154|                 "H": cb_entropy,
155|                 "used_codes": used_codes,
156|                 "indices": indices,
157|                 "group_indices": group_indices,
158|                 "avg_prob": avg_prob if self.soft_entropy else None,
159|             },
160|         )
161| 
162|     def soft_entropy_loss(self, z):
163|         group_code_book = self.group_codebook / (self.embed_dim ** 0.5 if self.l2_norm else 1)
164|         divided_z = rearrange(z, '... (g c) -> ... g c', c=self.group_size)
165| 
166|         distance = -2 * torch.einsum('... g c, d c ->... g d', divided_z, group_code_book)
167|         prob = (-distance * self.inv_temperature).softmax(dim=-1)
168|         if self.persample_entropy_compute == 'analytical':
169|             if self.l2_norm:
170|                 p = torch.sigmoid(-4 * z / (self.embed_dim ** 0.5) * self.inv_temperature)
171|             else:
172|                 p = torch.sigmoid(-4 * z * self.inv_temperature)
173|             prob = torch.stack([p, 1 - p], dim=-1)
174|             per_sample_entropy = self.get_entropy(prob, dim=-1, normalize=False).sum(dim=-1).mean()
175|         else:
176|             per_sample_entropy = self.get_entropy(prob, dim=-1, normalize=False).sum(dim=-1).mean()
177| 
178|         avg_prob = reduce(prob, '... g d ->g d', 'mean')
179|         codebook_entropy_val = self.get_entropy(avg_prob, dim=-1, normalize=False)
180| 
181|         return per_sample_entropy, codebook_entropy_val.sum(), avg_prob
182| 
183|     def get_hard_per_sample_entropy(self, zb_by_sample):
184|         probs_per_dim = zb_by_sample.sum(1) / zb_by_sample.shape[1]
185|         persample_entropy = (
186|             -probs_per_dim * torch.log(probs_per_dim + 1e-8)
187|             - (1 - probs_per_dim) * torch.log(1 - probs_per_dim + 1e-8)
188|         )
189|         persample_entropy = persample_entropy.sum(-1)
190|         return persample_entropy.mean()
191| 
192|     def codes_to_indexes(self, zhat):
193|         assert zhat.shape[-1] == self.embed_dim, f"Expected {self.embed_dim} dimensions, got {zhat.shape[-1]}"
194|         return ((zhat.to(torch.int64) + 1) // 2 * self.basis).sum(axis=-1)
195| 
196|     def codes_to_group_indexes(self, zhat):
197|         zhat_in_group = rearrange(zhat, 'b ... (g c) -> b ... g c', c=self.group_size)
198|         return ((zhat_in_group.to(torch.int64) + 1) // 2 * self.group_basis).sum(axis=-1).to(torch.int64)
199| 
200|     def indexes_to_codes(self, indices):
201|         indices = indices.unsqueeze(-1)
202|         codes_non_centered = torch.remainder(
203|             torch.floor_divide(indices, self.basis), 2
204|         )
205|         if codes_non_centered.shape[-1] == 64:
206|             codes_non_centered[..., :1] = 1 - codes_non_centered[..., :1]
207|         elif codes_non_centered.shape[-2] >= 64:
208|             raise NotImplementedError
209| 
210|         return codes_non_centered * 2 - 1
211| 
212|     def group_indexes_to_codes(self, group_indices):
213|         group_indices = group_indices.unsqueeze(-1)
214|         codes_non_centered = torch.remainder(
215|             torch.floor_divide(group_indices, self.group_basis), 2
216|         )
217|         codes_non_centered = rearrange(codes_non_centered, 'b ... g c -> b ... (g c)')
218|         return codes_non_centered * 2 - 1

1| """UniAR model: Qwen3-VL backbone + BSQ vision encoder + visual token prediction head."""
2| 
3| from typing import Optional
4| from contextlib import contextmanager
5| 
6| import torch
7| import torch.nn as nn
8| from transformers.generation import GenerationMixin
9| from transformers.models.qwen3_vl.modeling_qwen3_vl import (
10|     Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration,
11|     Qwen3VLModel,
12|     Qwen3VLPreTrainedModel,
13|     Qwen3VLTextDecoderLayer,
14|     Qwen3VLTextRMSNorm,
15| )
16| 
17| from uniar.configuration_uniar import UniARConfig
18| from uniar.vision_encoder.modeling_vision_encoder import UniARVisionModel
19| 
20| 
21| @contextmanager
22| def _skip_final_norm(text_model: nn.Module):
23|     """Swap ``text_model.norm`` for an ``nn.Identity`` for the duration of the block.
24| 
25|     During image-generation rollout, the ``output_layer_vistok`` head already
26|     applies its own RMSNorm as its first layer; stacking the backbone's final
27|     RMSNorm on top would differ from the training-time path. We temporarily
28|     bypass the backbone norm so the head sees the exact distribution it was
29|     trained on.
30|     """
31|     original = text_model.norm
32|     text_model.norm = nn.Identity()
33|     try:
34|         yield
35|     finally:
36|         text_model.norm = original
37| 
38| 
39| class UniARModel(Qwen3VLModel):
40|     """
41|     UniAR base model.
42| 
43|     Mirrors ``Qwen3VLModel`` but substitutes the vision tower with
44|     ``UniARVisionModel`` so BSQ-quantized visual tokens flow into the LLM.
45|     """
46| 
47|     config_class = UniARConfig
48| 
49|     def __init__(self, config: UniARConfig):
50|         super().__init__(config)
51|         del self.visual
52|         self.visual = UniARVisionModel._from_config(config.vision_config)
53| 
54| 
55| def _build_vistok_head(config: UniARConfig) -> nn.Module:
56|     vision_config = config.vision_config
57|     pred_level = 1 + len(vision_config.deepstack_visual_indexes)
58|     vispred_output_dim = (
59|         vision_config.bsq_dim * 2 * vision_config.spatial_merge_size ** 2 * pred_level
60|     )
61|     hidden_size = config.text_config.hidden_size
62| 
63|     if config.vistok_pred_use_mlp:
64|         middle_dim = 16 * 1024
65|         return nn.Sequential(
66|             Qwen3VLTextRMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=config.text_config.rms_norm_eps),
67|             nn.Linear(hidden_size, middle_dim, bias=False),
68|             nn.GELU(approximate="tanh"),
69|             nn.Linear(middle_dim, vispred_output_dim, bias=False),
70|         )
71|     if config.vistok_pred_layernorm:
72|         return nn.Sequential(
73|             Qwen3VLTextRMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=config.text_config.rms_norm_eps),
74|             nn.Linear(hidden_size, vispred_output_dim, bias=False),
75|         )
76|     return nn.Linear(hidden_size, vispred_output_dim, bias=False)

79| class UniARForConditionalGeneration(Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration):
80|     """
81|     UniAR conditional generation model.
82| 
83|     Extends ``Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`` with:
84| 
85|     - ``model.visual`` swapped for ``UniARVisionModel`` (BSQ).
86|     - Optional ``output_layer_vistok`` head for visual-token (BSQ bit) prediction.
87|     - Optional ``visual_decoder`` — a small stack of text decoder layers applied
88|       on top of the LLM hidden states before the visual-token head.
89|     - ``generation_mode`` selector (``'text'`` vs ``'image'``) used by the
90|       generation loop to route through either ``lm_head`` or
91|       ``output_layer_vistok``.
92|     """
93| 
94|     config_class = UniARConfig
95| 
96|     def __init__(self, config: UniARConfig):
97|         Qwen3VLPreTrainedModel.__init__(self, config)
98|         GenerationMixin.__init__(self)
99|         self.model = UniARModel(config)
100|         self.lm_head = nn.Linear(
101|             config.text_config.hidden_size,
102|             config.text_config.vocab_size,
103|             bias=False,
104|         )
105|         self.rope_deltas = None
106| 
107|         if config.vistok_pred:
108|             self.output_layer_vistok = _build_vistok_head(config)
109|             if config.visual_transformer_decoder:
110|                 self.visual_decoder = nn.ModuleList(

113|                         for layer_idx in range(config.visual_transformer_decoder_depth)
114|                     ]
115|                 )
116| 
117|         self.generation_mode = "text"
118|         self.post_init()

120|     def set_generation_mode(self, mode: str) -> None:
121|         if mode not in ("text", "image"):
122|             raise ValueError(f"Invalid generation mode: {mode}")
123|         self.generation_mode = mode
124| 
125|     def visual_transformer_pred(
126|         self,
127|         hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
128|         attention_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
129|         position_ids: Optional[torch.LongTensor] = None,

1| """
2| UniAR vision encoder: Qwen3-VL vision backbone + Binary Spherical Quantization.
3| """
4| 
5| from typing import Optional, Tuple, List
6| 
7| import numpy as np
8| import torch
9| import torch.nn as nn
10| import torch.nn.functional as F
11| 
12| from transformers.models.qwen3_vl.modeling_qwen3_vl import Qwen3VLVisionModel
13| 
14| from .bsq import BinarySphericalQuantizer
15| from .configuration_vision_encoder import UniARVisionConfig
16| 
17| 
18| class UniARPatchMerger(nn.Module):
19|     """
20|     A Qwen3-VL-compatible patch merger with configurable middle dim.
21| 
22|     Parameter layout matches Qwen3VLVisionPatchMerger (norm, linear_fc1, linear_fc2),
23|     but supports an independent ``mid_size`` for the MLP bottleneck so the same
24|     module can act as the main merger or as a BSQ input/output projection.
25|     """
26| 
27|     def __init__(
28|         self,
29|         dim: int,
30|         context_dim: int,
31|         spatial_merge_size: int = 2,
32|         use_postshuffle_norm: bool = False,
33|         mid_size: Optional[int] = None,
34|     ) -> None:
35|         super().__init__()
36|         self.hidden_size = context_dim * (spatial_merge_size ** 2)
37|         if mid_size is None:
38|             mid_size = self.hidden_size
39|         self.use_postshuffle_norm = use_postshuffle_norm
40|         norm_dim = self.hidden_size if use_postshuffle_norm else context_dim
41|         self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(norm_dim, eps=1e-6)
42|         self.linear_fc1 = nn.Linear(self.hidden_size, mid_size)
43|         self.act_fn = nn.GELU()
44|         self.linear_fc2 = nn.Linear(mid_size, dim)
45| 
46|     def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
47|         if self.use_postshuffle_norm:
48|             x = self.norm(x.reshape(-1, self.hidden_size))
49|         else:
50|             x = self.norm(x).reshape(-1, self.hidden_size)
51|         x = self.linear_fc2(self.act_fn(self.linear_fc1(x)))
52|         return x
53| 
54| 
55| class UniARVisionModel(Qwen3VLVisionModel):
56|     """
57|     UniAR vision encoder.
58| 
59|     Extends ``Qwen3VLVisionModel`` with Binary Spherical Quantization (BSQ) between
60|     the transformer blocks and the patch merger, producing discrete visual tokens
61|     used by the UniAR autoregressive head.
62| 
63|     When ``config.use_bsq`` is ``False`` this behaves as a drop-in Qwen3-VL vision
64|     encoder.
65|     """
66| 
67|     config_class = UniARVisionConfig
68| 
69|     def __init__(self, config: UniARVisionConfig, *inputs, no_merger: bool = False, **kwargs) -> None:
70|         super().__init__(config, *inputs, **kwargs)
71| 
72|         if no_merger:
73|             del self.merger
74| 
75|         if config.use_bsq:
76|             use_postshuffle_norm = not config.bsq_skip_final_layernorm
77|             if not no_merger:
78|                 del self.merger
79|                 self.merger = UniARPatchMerger(
80|                     dim=config.out_hidden_size,
81|                     context_dim=config.hidden_size,
82|                     spatial_merge_size=config.spatial_merge_size,
83|                     use_postshuffle_norm=use_postshuffle_norm,
84|                 )
85|             self._init_bsq_params()
86|             for idx in range(len(config.deepstack_visual_indexes)):
87|                 self._init_bsq_params(multiscale_idx=idx)
88| 
89|     def _init_bsq_params(self, multiscale_idx: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
90|         config = self.config
91|         bsq_dim = config.bsq_dim
92|         if multiscale_idx is None:
93|             self.bsq = BinarySphericalQuantizer(bsq_dim, input_format='c_last', gamma=0.5)
94| 
95|         bsq_input_proj = UniARPatchMerger(
96|             dim=bsq_dim,
97|             context_dim=config.hidden_size,
98|             spatial_merge_size=1,
99|             use_postshuffle_norm=True,
100|             mid_size=config.bsq_hidden_dim,
101|         )
102|         bsq_out_proj = UniARPatchMerger(
103|             dim=config.hidden_size,
104|             context_dim=bsq_dim,
105|             spatial_merge_size=1,
106|             use_postshuffle_norm=True,
107|             mid_size=config.bsq_hidden_dim,
108|         )
109| 
110|         input_name = 'bsq_input_proj' if multiscale_idx is None else f'bsq_input_proj_list_{multiscale_idx}'
111|         output_name = 'bsq_output_proj' if multiscale_idx is None else f'bsq_output_proj_list_{multiscale_idx}'
112|         setattr(self, input_name, bsq_input_proj)
113|         setattr(self, output_name, bsq_out_proj)
114| 
115|     def bsq_quantize(
116|         self,
117|         hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
118|         multiscale_idx: Optional[int] = None,
119|         direct_indices: bool = False,
120|         bsq_flip_prob: float = 0.0,
121|         bsq_flip_level: str = "per_batch",
122|     ) -> torch.Tensor:
123|         input_name = 'bsq_input_proj' if multiscale_idx is None else f'bsq_input_proj_list_{multiscale_idx}'
124|         output_name = 'bsq_output_proj' if multiscale_idx is None else f'bsq_output_proj_list_{multiscale_idx}'
125| 
126|         bsq_input_layer = getattr(self, input_name)
127|         bsq_output_layer = getattr(self, output_name)
128| 
129|         zq = bsq_input_layer(hidden_states)
130|         if isinstance(zq, tuple):
131|             zq = zq[0] + zq[1] if zq[1] is not None else zq[0]
132| 
133|         if bsq_flip_level == "per_bit" and bsq_flip_prob > 0.0:
134|             noise_apply_strength = np.random.randint(0, int(100 * bsq_flip_prob + 1)) * 0.01
135|             mask = (torch.rand(*zq.shape) < noise_apply_strength).to(zq)
136|             zq = zq * (1 - mask) + -zq * mask
137| 
138|         zq = F.normalize(zq, dim=-1)
139|         zq, _bsq_loss, meta = self.bsq(zq)
140| 
141|         bsq_indices = meta.get('indices', None)
142|         if bsq_indices is not None and not self.training:
143|             zq = self.bsq.get_codebook_entry(meta['indices']).bfloat16()
144|             if direct_indices:
145|                 bsq_indices_gt = (self.bsq.indexes_to_codes(bsq_indices) + 1) // 2
146|                 bsq_indices_gt = bsq_indices_gt.reshape(-1, bsq_indices_gt.shape[-1] * self.spatial_merge_unit)
147|                 return bsq_indices_gt
148| 
149|         hidden_states = bsq_output_layer(zq)
150|         if isinstance(hidden_states, tuple):
151|             hidden_states = hidden_states[0] + hidden_states[1] if hidden_states[1] is not None else hidden_states[0]
152|         return hidden_states
153| 
154|     def bsq_indices_to_features(
155|         self,
156|         vistok_pred: torch.Tensor,
157|         multiscale_idx='all',
158|         spatial_merge_unit: Optional[int] = None,
159|         with_merger: bool = False,
160|         inference_skip_final_layernorm: bool = False,
161|     ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, List[torch.Tensor]]:
162|         if multiscale_idx == 'all':
163|             idx_list = [None] + list(range(len(self.config.deepstack_visual_indexes)))
164|         else:
165|             idx_list = [multiscale_idx]
166| 
167|         if spatial_merge_unit is None:
168|             spatial_merge_unit = self.spatial_merge_unit
169| 
170|         vistok_shape = (-1, len(idx_list), spatial_merge_unit, self.config.bsq_dim)
171|         vistok_pred = vistok_pred.view(*vistok_shape).bfloat16()
172|         zq = self.bsq.get_group_codebook_entry(vistok_pred).bfloat16()
173| 
174|         zq_list = [zq[:, i] for i in range(len(idx_list))] if multiscale_idx == 'all' else [zq]
175| 
176|         hidden_states: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
177|         processed_deepstack_list: List[torch.Tensor] = []
178| 
179|         for i, ms_idx in enumerate(idx_list):
180|             zq_i = zq_list[i]
181|             output_name = 'bsq_output_proj' if ms_idx is None else f'bsq_output_proj_list_{ms_idx}'
182|             bsq_output_layer = getattr(self, output_name)
183|             hs = bsq_output_layer(zq_i)
184| 
185|             if (
186|                 self.config.bsq_skip_final_layernorm
187|                 and not inference_skip_final_layernorm
188|                 and ms_idx is not None
189|             ):
190|                 hs = self.merger.norm(hs)
191| 
192|             if ms_idx is None:
193|                 if with_merger:
194|                     hs = self.merger(hs)
195|                 hidden_states = hs
196|             else:
197|                 if with_merger:
198|                     hs = self.deepstack_merger_list[ms_idx](hs)
199|                 processed_deepstack_list.append(hs)
200| 
201|         return hidden_states, processed_deepstack_list
202| 
203|     def forward(
204|         self,
205|         hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
206|         grid_thw: torch.Tensor,
207|         bsq_only: bool = False,
208|         bsq_feature_level: Optional[int] = None,
209|         direct_indices: bool = False,
210|         bsq_flip_prob: float = 0.0,
211|         bsq_flip_level: str = "per_batch",
212|         **kwargs,
213|     ):
214|         hidden_states = self.patch_embed(hidden_states)
215| 
216|         pos_embeds = self.fast_pos_embed_interpolate(grid_thw)
217|         hidden_states = hidden_states + pos_embeds
218| 
219|         rotary_pos_emb = self.rot_pos_emb(grid_thw)
220|         seq_len, _ = hidden_states.size()
221|         hidden_states = hidden_states.reshape(seq_len, -1)
222|         rotary_pos_emb = rotary_pos_emb.reshape(seq_len, -1)
223|         emb = torch.cat((rotary_pos_emb, rotary_pos_emb), dim=-1)
224|         position_embeddings = (emb.cos(), emb.sin())
225| 
226|         cu_seqlens = torch.repeat_interleave(
227|             grid_thw[:, 1] * grid_thw[:, 2],
228|             grid_thw[:, 0],
229|         ).cumsum(
230|             dim=0,
231|             dtype=grid_thw.dtype if torch.jit.is_tracing() else torch.int32,
232|         )
233|         cu_seqlens = F.pad(cu_seqlens, (1, 0), value=0)
234| 
235|         raw_deepstack_states: List[torch.Tensor] = []
236|         for layer_num, blk in enumerate(self.blocks):
237|             hidden_states = blk(
238|                 hidden_states,
239|                 cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
240|                 position_embeddings=position_embeddings,
241|                 **kwargs,
242|             )
243|             if layer_num in self.deepstack_visual_indexes:
244|                 raw_deepstack_states.append(hidden_states)
245| 
246|         if self.config.use_bsq:
247|             hidden_states = self.bsq_quantize(
248|                 hidden_states,
249|                 multiscale_idx=None,
250|                 direct_indices=direct_indices,
251|                 bsq_flip_prob=bsq_flip_prob,
252|                 bsq_flip_level=bsq_flip_level,
253|             )
254|             processed_deepstack: List[torch.Tensor] = []
255|             for idx, x in enumerate(raw_deepstack_states):
256|                 x = self.bsq_quantize(
257|                     x,
258|                     multiscale_idx=idx,
259|                     direct_indices=direct_indices,
260|                     bsq_flip_prob=bsq_flip_prob,
261|                     bsq_flip_level=bsq_flip_level,
262|                 )
263|                 if not bsq_only and self.config.bsq_skip_final_layernorm:
264|                     x = self.merger.norm(x)
265|                 processed_deepstack.append(x)
266|             raw_deepstack_states = processed_deepstack
267| 
268|             if bsq_only:
269|                 if bsq_feature_level is None:
270|                     return hidden_states, processed_deepstack
271|                 combined = [hidden_states] + processed_deepstack
272|                 return combined[bsq_feature_level], []
273| 
274|         if bsq_only:
275|             return hidden_states, []
276| 
277|         hidden_states = self.merger(hidden_states)
278|         deepstack_feature_lists: List[torch.Tensor] = []
279|         for idx, x in enumerate(raw_deepstack_states):
280|             deepstack_feature_lists.append(self.deepstack_merger_list[idx](x))
281| 
282|         return hidden_states, deepstack_feature_lists
283|

286| # BSQ image tokenizer loader

289| 
290| def _convert_img_to_patch(img: torch.Tensor):
291|     """Convert a BCHW image batch to the flattened patch layout UniAR expects."""
292|     spatial_patch_size = 16
293|     temporal_patch_size = 2
294|     spatial_merge_size = 1
295| 
296|     bs, c, h, w = img.shape
297|     grid_t = 1
298|     grid_h = h // spatial_merge_size // spatial_patch_size
299|     grid_w = w // spatial_merge_size // spatial_patch_size
300| 
301|     img = img.unsqueeze(2).expand(-1, -1, temporal_patch_size, -1, -1)
302|     flatten_image = img.reshape(
303|         bs,
304|         c,
305|         grid_t,
306|         temporal_patch_size,
307|         grid_h // spatial_merge_size,
308|         spatial_merge_size,
309|         spatial_patch_size,
310|         grid_w // spatial_merge_size,
311|         spatial_merge_size,
312|         spatial_patch_size,
313|     )
314|     flatten_image = flatten_image.permute(0, 2, 4, 7, 5, 8, 1, 3, 6, 9).reshape(
315|         bs * grid_t * grid_h * grid_w, -1
316|     )
317| 
318|     grid_thw = torch.tensor([[grid_t, grid_h, grid_w]] * bs).to(flatten_image.device)
319|     return flatten_image, grid_thw
320| 
321| 
322| def load_bsq_image_tokenizer_and_transform(
323|     model_path: str,
324|     resolution: int | None = None,
325|     feature_level=None,
326|     no_merger: bool = False,
327|     subfolder: str | None = None,
328| ):
329|     """
330|     Load a UniAR vision encoder as a BSQ image tokenizer.
331| 
332|     Args:
333|         model_path: Path or HF id of a saved UniARVisionModel checkpoint.
334|         resolution: Deprecated compatibility argument; loading is resolution-independent.
335|         feature_level: Which BSQ feature level to use (``None`` = all concatenated).
336|         no_merger: Skip the final merger (useful when only BSQ indices are needed).
337|         subfolder: Optional checkpoint subfolder, useful for packaged HF repos.
338| 
339|     Returns:
340|         The loaded ``UniARVisionModel`` with ``embed_dim`` and
341|         ``convert_img_to_patch`` attached for downstream consumers.
342|     """
343|     config_kwargs = {}
344|     if subfolder is not None:
345|         config_kwargs["subfolder"] = subfolder
346| 
347|     config = UniARVisionConfig.from_pretrained(model_path, **config_kwargs)
348| 
349|     model_kwargs = {
350|         "config": config,
351|         "torch_dtype": torch.bfloat16,
352|         "no_merger": no_merger,
353|         "ignore_mismatched_sizes": True,
354|     }
355|     if subfolder is not None:
356|         model_kwargs["subfolder"] = subfolder
357| 
358|     tokenizer = UniARVisionModel.from_pretrained(
359|         model_path,
360|         **model_kwargs,
361|     )
362|     tokenizer.is_moe = False
363|     tokenizer.convert_img_to_patch = _convert_img_to_patch
364| 
365|     if not tokenizer.config.deepstack_visual_indexes:

367|     elif feature_level is None:
368|         tokenizer.embed_dim = tokenizer.config.hidden_size * (1 + len(tokenizer.config.deepstack_visual_indexes))
369|     elif feature_level in (0, 1, 2, 3):
370|         tokenizer.embed_dim = tokenizer.config.hidden_size
371|     else:
372|         raise NotImplementedError(f"Unsupported feature_level {feature_level}")
373| 
374|     return tokenizer

63|

65|     projection that maps BSQ encoder features to the DiT hidden dim and adds
66|     them to the patchified latent before transformer blocks.
67|     """

69|     @register_to_config
70|     def __init__(

138|     def prepare_siglip_tensor(

142|     ) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
143|         """Project and optionally upsample BSQ features for latent injection.
144| 
145|         Args:
146|             siglip_tensor: BSQ features, shape ``(B, seq_len, C)``.
147|             target_spatial_size: ``(target_h, target_w)`` after upsampling.

155|         # CFG dropout during training

159|             random_tensor = siglip_tensor.new_empty(shape).bernoulli_(keep_prob)

172|             ):

174|             else:
175|                 grid_size = int(seq_len**0.5)
176|                 grid_h, grid_w = grid_size, grid_size
177| 
178|             siglip_tensor = siglip_tensor.reshape(bs, grid_h, grid_w, channel)
179|             siglip_tensor = siglip_tensor.permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
180| 
181|             if target_spatial_size is not None:
182|                 target_h, target_w = target_spatial_size
183|             else:
184|                 target_h = grid_h * int(self.upscale_factor)
185|                 target_w = grid_w * int(self.upscale_factor)
186| 
187|             siglip_tensor = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(
188|                 siglip_tensor,
189|                 size=(target_h, target_w),
190|                 mode="bicubic",
191|                 align_corners=False,
192|             )
193|             siglip_tensor = siglip_tensor.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)
194|             siglip_tensor = siglip_tensor.reshape(bs, -1, channel)
195| 
196|         return self.siglip_embed_add_latent(siglip_tensor)
197| 
198|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------
199|     # Random crop positional embedding helpers (training only)
200|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------
201| 
202|     def _sample_random_crop_offset(self, height: int, width: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
203|         """Sample random crop offset for positional embeddings during training."""
204|         patch_size = self.pos_embed.patch_size
205|         pos_embed_max_size = self.pos_embed.pos_embed_max_size
206| 
207|         grid_h = height // patch_size
208|         grid_w = width // patch_size
209| 
210|         if self.random_crop_pos_embed_max_grid is not None:
211|             effective_max_size = min(
212|                 self.random_crop_pos_embed_max_grid, pos_embed_max_size
213|             )
214|         else:
215|             effective_max_size = pos_embed_max_size
216| 
217|         center_offset_top = (pos_embed_max_size - effective_max_size) // 2
218|         center_offset_left = (pos_embed_max_size - effective_max_size) // 2
219| 
220|         max_top = max(0, effective_max_size - grid_h)
221|         max_left = max(0, effective_max_size - grid_w)
222| 
223|         top = center_offset_top + random.randint(0, max_top)
224|         left = center_offset_left + random.randint(0, max_left)
225| 
226|         return (top, left)
227| 
228|     def _get_cropped_pos_embed(
229|         self, height: int, width: int, crop_offset: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None
230|     ) -> torch.Tensor:
231|         """Get cropped positional embeddings (random or center crop)."""
232|         patch_size = self.pos_embed.patch_size
233|         pos_embed_max_size = self.pos_embed.pos_embed_max_size
234| 
235|         grid_h = height // patch_size
236|         grid_w = width // patch_size
237| 
238|         if crop_offset is None:
239|             top = (pos_embed_max_size - grid_h) // 2
240|             left = (pos_embed_max_size - grid_w) // 2
241|         else:
242|             top, left = crop_offset
243| 
244|         spatial_pos_embed = self.pos_embed.pos_embed.reshape(
245|             1, pos_embed_max_size, pos_embed_max_size, -1
246|         )
247|         spatial_pos_embed = spatial_pos_embed[
248|             :, top : top + grid_h, left : left + grid_w, :
249|         ]
250|         return spatial_pos_embed.reshape(1, -1, spatial_pos_embed.shape[-1])
251| 
252|     def _apply_pos_embed(
253|         self, latent: torch.Tensor, crop_offset: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None
254|     ) -> torch.Tensor:
255|         """Apply patch embedding + positional embedding with optional random crop."""
256|         height, width = latent.shape[-2:]
257| 
258|         latent = self.pos_embed.proj(latent)
259|         if self.pos_embed.flatten:
260|             latent = latent.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
261|         if self.pos_embed.layer_norm:
262|             latent = self.pos_embed.norm(latent)
263| 
264|         if self.pos_embed.pos_embed is None:
265|             return latent.to(latent.dtype)
266| 
267|         pos_embed = self._get_cropped_pos_embed(height, width, crop_offset)
268|         return (latent + pos_embed).to(latent.dtype)
269| 
270|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------
271|     # Forward
272|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------
273| 
274|     def forward(
275|         self,
276|         hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
277|         encoder_hidden_states: torch.Tensor = None,
278|         pooled_projections: torch.Tensor = None,
279|         timestep: torch.LongTensor = None,
280|         block_controlnet_hidden_states: Optional[List] = None,
281|         joint_attention_kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
282|         return_dict: bool = True,
283|         skip_layers: Optional[List[int]] = None,
284|         siglip_tensor: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
285|     ) -> Union[torch.Tensor, Transformer2DModelOutput]:
286|         if joint_attention_kwargs is not None:
287|             joint_attention_kwargs = joint_attention_kwargs.copy()
288|             lora_scale = joint_attention_kwargs.pop("scale", 1.0)
289|         else:
290|             lora_scale = 1.0
291| 
292|         if USE_PEFT_BACKEND:
293|             scale_lora_layers(self, lora_scale)
294|         else:
295|             if (
296|                 joint_attention_kwargs is not None
297|                 and joint_attention_kwargs.get("scale", None) is not None
298|             ):
299|                 logger.warning(
300|                     "Passing `scale` via `joint_attention_kwargs` when not using "
301|                     "the PEFT backend is ineffective."
302|                 )
303| 
304|         height, width = hidden_states.shape[-2:]
305| 
306|         # Compute target spatial size for siglip upsampling

1| """
2| Simple UniAR text-to-image generation example.
3| 
4| This script loads a packaged UniAR checkpoint, generates one image from one
5| prompt, and saves it as a PNG.
6| 
7| Example:
8|     python inference/generate.py \
9|         --model_path /path/to/UniAR \
10|         --prompt "A cute anime girl." \
11|         --output_path inference/generated.png
12| """
13| 
14| import argparse
15| import os
16| import sys
17| 
18| import torch
19| 
20| _REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
21| if _REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:
22|     sys.path.insert(0, _REPO_ROOT)
23| 
24| from transformers import AutoProcessor
25| 
26| from uniar import UniARForConditionalGeneration, UniARVisualDecoder
27| 
28| from inference.visual_inputs import prepare_visual_inputs
29| 
30| def main(args):
31|     device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
32|     print(f"device: {device}")
33|     print(f"loading model: {args.model_path}")
34|     attn_implementation = args.attn
35| 
36|     ar_model = UniARForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
37|         args.model_path,
38|         torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
39|         attn_implementation=attn_implementation,
40|     ).to(device)
41|     ar_model.eval()
42| 
43|     ar_processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(args.model_path, padding_side="left")
44|     visual_decoder = UniARVisualDecoder.from_pretrained(args.model_path, device=device)
45| 
46|     ar_height = args.ar_height
47|     ar_width = args.ar_width
48|     upsampling_ratio = args.upsampling_ratio
49| 
50|     visual_inputs = prepare_visual_inputs(
51|         [args.prompt], ar_model, ar_processor,
52|         ar_height, ar_width,
53|     )
54|     generated_visual_ids = ar_model.generate_visual(
55|         prefix_input_ids=visual_inputs["prefix_input_ids"],
56|         attention_mask=visual_inputs["attention_mask"],
57|         pos_ids_image=visual_inputs["pos_ids_image"],
58|         pos_ids_all=visual_inputs["pos_ids_all"],
59|         image_token_num=visual_inputs["image_token_num"],
60|         temperature=args.temperature,
61|         cfg=args.cfg,
62|         show_progress=True,
63|     )
64| 
65|     images = visual_decoder.decode(
66|         generated_visual_ids,
67|         ar_height=ar_height,
68|         ar_width=ar_width,
69|         upsampling_ratio=upsampling_ratio,
70|         num_inference_steps=args.decoder_num_inference_steps,
71|         guidance_scale=args.decoder_cfg_scale,
72|     )
73| 
74|     output_dir = os.path.dirname(args.output_path)
75|     if output_dir:
76|         os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
77|     images[0].save(args.output_path)
78|     print(f"saved image: {args.output_path}")
79| 
80| 
81| if __name__ == "__main__":
82|     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Simple UniAR text-to-image generation example")
83|     parser.add_argument("--model_path", required=True, help="Local or HF path of UniAR checkpoint")
84|     parser.add_argument("--prompt", required=True, help="a cute anime girl.")
85|     parser.add_argument("--output_path", default="inference/generated.png")
86|     parser.add_argument("--ar_height", type=int, default=960, help="AR visual-token rollout height")
87|     parser.add_argument("--ar_width", type=int, default=960, help="AR visual-token rollout width")
88|     parser.add_argument("--image_height", type=int, default=None,
89|                         help="Deprecated alias of --ar_height")
90|     parser.add_argument("--image_width", type=int, default=None,
91|                         help="Deprecated alias of --ar_width")
92|     parser.add_argument("--upsampling_ratio", type=float, default=1.067,
93|                         help="SD3 decoder upsampling ratio from AR resolution to output resolution.")
94|     parser.add_argument("--temperature", type=float, default=1.0)
95|     parser.add_argument("--cfg", type=float, default=1.5)
96|     parser.add_argument("--decoder_num_inference_steps", type=int, default=28)

1| """
2| Input preparation helpers for UniAR visual generation.
3| """
4| 
5| from typing import List, Optional
6| 
7| import torch
8| from PIL import Image
9| 
10| from uniar import CHAT_TEMPLATE
11| 
12| try:
13|     from qwen_vl_utils import process_vision_info as _qwen_process_vision_info
14| except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover -- only needed for edit mode
15|     _qwen_process_vision_info = None
16| 
17| 
18| def _build_visual_messages(
19|     prompt: str,
20|     ar_height: int,
21|     ar_width: int,
22|     downsample_factor: int,
23|     input_image: Optional[Image.Image] = None,
24| ):
25|     content = [{"type": "text", "text": prompt}]
26|     if input_image is not None:
27|         # Edit mode: input image goes between the instruction and the
28|         # "<image_gen> ..." marker. Both cond and uncond branches carry the
29|         # image — CFG is over text only, not over image conditioning.
30|         content.append({"type": "image", "image": input_image})
31|     content.append(
32|         {
33|             "type": "text",
34|             "text": (
35|                 f"<image_gen> generate image "
36|                 f"{ar_height // downsample_factor} {ar_width // downsample_factor}"
37|             ),
38|         }
39|     )
40|     return [{"role": "user", "content": content}]
41| 
42| 
43| def prepare_visual_inputs(
44|     prompts: List[str],
45|     ar_model,
46|     ar_processor,
47|     ar_height: int,
48|     ar_width: int,
49|     input_images: Optional[List[Image.Image]] = None,
50| ):
51|     """Build a 2B left-padded prefix and mRoPE ids for visual generation.
52| 
53|     Returns a dict with tensor names expected by
54|     ``UniARForConditionalGeneration.generate_visual``:
55| 
56|     - ``prefix_input_ids``: conditional + unconditional prefix ids, shape ``(2B, L)``
57|     - ``attention_mask``: prefix attention mask, shape ``(2B, L)``
58|     - ``pos_ids_all``: mRoPE ids for prefix + generated visual tokens
59|     - ``pos_ids_image``: mRoPE ids for generated visual tokens only
60|     - ``image_token_num``: number of visual tokens to generate
61| 
62|     When ``input_images`` is provided, edit mode is enabled. Each prompt must
63|     have one PIL image. The image is carried by both the conditional and
64|     unconditional branches, so CFG only changes the text condition.
65|     """
66|     v_cfg = ar_model.config.vision_config
67|     patch = v_cfg.patch_size
68|     merge = v_cfg.spatial_merge_size
69|     downsample_factor = patch * merge
70| 
71|     is_edit = input_images is not None
72|     if is_edit:
73|         assert len(input_images) == len(prompts), (
74|             f"len(input_images) ({len(input_images)}) must match len(prompts) ({len(prompts)})"
75|         )
76|         if _qwen_process_vision_info is None:
77|             raise ImportError(
78|                 "qwen_vl_utils is required for edit mode. "
79|                 "Install via `pip install qwen-vl-utils`."
80|             )
81| 
82|     cond_messages = [
83|         _build_visual_messages(
84|             prompt,
85|             ar_height,
86|             ar_width,
87|             downsample_factor,
88|             input_image=(input_images[i] if is_edit else None),
89|         )
90|         for i, prompt in enumerate(prompts)
91|     ]
92|     uncond_messages = [
93|         _build_visual_messages(
94|             "",
95|             ar_height,
96|             ar_width,
97|             downsample_factor,
98|             input_image=(input_images[i] if is_edit else None),
99|         )
100|         for i in range(len(prompts))
101|     ]
102|     all_messages = cond_messages + uncond_messages
103| 
104|     ar_processor.chat_template = CHAT_TEMPLATE
105|     texts = ar_processor.apply_chat_template(
106|         all_messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True
107|     )
108|     texts = [text + "<|vision_start|>" for text in texts]
109| 
110|     if is_edit:
111|         image_inputs, video_inputs = _qwen_process_vision_info(all_messages)
112|         inputs = ar_processor(
113|             text=texts,
114|             images=image_inputs,
115|             videos=video_inputs,
116|             padding=True,
117|             return_tensors="pt",
118|         ).to(ar_model.device)
119|     else:
120|         inputs = ar_processor(
121|             text=texts,
122|             padding=True,
123|             return_tensors="pt",
124|         ).to(ar_model.device)
125| 
126|     prefix_input_ids = inputs.input_ids
127|     attention_mask = inputs.attention_mask
128| 
129|     batch_size_2 = prefix_input_ids.shape[0]
130|     image_token_num = (ar_height // downsample_factor) * (ar_width // downsample_factor)
131|     image_input_ids = torch.full(
132|         (batch_size_2, image_token_num),
133|         ar_model.config.image_token_id,
134|         device=ar_model.device,
135|         dtype=torch.long,
136|     )
137|     output_image_grid_thw = torch.tensor(
138|         [[1, ar_height // patch, ar_width // patch]] * batch_size_2,
139|         device=ar_model.device,
140|         dtype=torch.long,
141|     )
142|     attention_mask_all = torch.cat(
143|         [attention_mask, torch.ones_like(image_input_ids)], dim=1
144|     )
145| 
146|     if is_edit:
147|         # get_rope_index needs per-image grid_thw for BOTH the input image and
148|         # the output image. Interleave per sample:
149|         # [input_grid_b0, output_grid_b0, input_grid_b1, output_grid_b1, ...].
150|         input_image_grid_thw = inputs.image_grid_thw
151|         combined_rows = []
152|         for i in range(batch_size_2):
153|             combined_rows.append(input_image_grid_thw[i: i + 1])
154|             combined_rows.append(output_image_grid_thw[i: i + 1])

1| """Reward functions for GRPO RL training.
2| 
3| Each function takes ``(images: List[PIL.Image], **kwargs)`` and returns a list
4| of reward scores (``None`` for samples where the reward does not apply, e.g.
5| a geneval reward on a non-geneval prompt).
6| 
7| Supported rewards:
8| - ``hpsv2_reward``         : human preference score v2 (applies to all samples)
9| - ``geneval_reward``       : GenEval task check (task == 'geneval' only)
10| - ``ocr_reward``           : OCR word-recall (task == 'ocr' only)
11| - ``unified_reward``       : generic VLM judge via vLLM (applies to all samples)
12| 
13| Each reward hits an HTTP endpoint configured via its ``*_API_ADDRESS`` env var
14| (or ``api_address`` kwarg). See ``reward_server/<name>/README.md`` for how to
15| start each server.
16| """
17| 
18| import io
19| import logging
20| import os
21| import pickle
22| import time
23| 
24| import requests
25| 
26| from reward_server.unified_reward.client import evaluate_batch
27| 
28| logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
29| 
30| 
31| def _post_with_retry(url, data, timeout=600, max_retries=3):
32|     for attempt in range(max_retries):
33|         try:
34|             resp = requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=timeout)
35|             resp.raise_for_status()
36|             return pickle.loads(resp.content)
37|         except Exception as e:
38|             if attempt < max_retries - 1:
39|                 wait = 5 * (attempt + 1)
40|                 logger.warning(f"[reward] request failed (attempt {attempt+1}/{max_retries}): {e}, retrying in {wait}s")
41|                 time.sleep(wait)
42|             else:
43|                 raise
44| 
45| 
46| def hpsv2_reward(images, **kwargs):
47|     """HPS v2.1 human-preference reward. Applies to all samples."""
48|     api_address = kwargs.get("api_address", os.environ.get("HPSV2_API_ADDRESS"))
49|     jpeg_data = []
50|     for image in images:
51|         buffer = io.BytesIO()
52|         if image.mode != "RGB":
53|             image = image.convert("RGB")
54|         image.save(buffer, format="JPEG")
55|         jpeg_data.append(buffer.getvalue())
56| 
57|     raw_prompts = kwargs.get("raw_prompt")
58|     payload = {"images": jpeg_data, "prompts": raw_prompts}
59|     result = _post_with_retry(api_address, pickle.dumps(payload))
60|     return result["scores"]
61| 
62| 
63| def geneval_reward(images, **kwargs):
64|     """GenEval compositional task-check reward. Only applies to task == 'geneval'."""
65|     api_address = kwargs.get("api_address", os.environ.get("GENEVAL_API_ADDRESS"))
66|     only_strict = kwargs.get("only_strict", False)
67| 
68|     tasks = kwargs.get("task")
69|     raw_prompts = kwargs.get("raw_prompt")
70|     metadatas = kwargs.get("metadata")
71| 
72|     if "geneval" not in tasks:
73|         return [None for _ in range(len(images))]
74| 
75|     geneval_images, geneval_metadatas, geneval_idx = [], [], []
76|     for idx, (img, t, raw_p, meta) in enumerate(zip(images, tasks, raw_prompts, metadatas)):
77|         if t != "geneval":
78|             continue
79|         buffer = io.BytesIO()
80|         if img.mode != "RGB":
81|             img = img.convert("RGB")
82|         img.save(buffer, format="JPEG")
83|         geneval_images.append(buffer.getvalue())
84|         meta["prompt"] = raw_p
85|         geneval_metadatas.append(meta)
86|         geneval_idx.append(idx)
87| 
88|     data = {"images": geneval_images, "meta_datas": geneval_metadatas, "only_strict": only_strict}
89|     response_data = _post_with_retry(api_address, pickle.dumps(data))
90| 
91|     geneval_rewards = response_data["scores"]
92| 
93|     rewards = [None for _ in range(len(images))]
94|     for idx, reward in zip(geneval_idx, geneval_rewards):
95|         rewards[idx] = reward
96|     return rewards
97| 
98| 
99| def ocr_reward(images, **kwargs):
100|     """OCR word-recall reward via PaddleOCR server. Only applies to task == 'ocr'."""
101|     api_address = kwargs.get("api_address", os.environ.get("OCR_API_ADDRESS"))
102|     tasks = kwargs.get("task")
103|     raw_prompts = kwargs.get("raw_prompt")
104| 
105|     if "ocr" not in tasks:
106|         return [None for _ in range(len(images))]
107| 
108|     ocr_images, ocr_prompts, ocr_idx = [], [], []
109|     for idx, (img, t, raw_p) in enumerate(zip(images, tasks, raw_prompts)):
110|         if t != "ocr":
111|             continue
112|         buffer = io.BytesIO()
113|         if img.mode != "RGB":
114|             img = img.convert("RGB")
115|         img.save(buffer, format="JPEG")
116|         ocr_images.append(buffer.getvalue())
117|         ocr_prompts.append(raw_p)
118|         ocr_idx.append(idx)
119| 
120|     payload = {"images": ocr_images, "prompts": ocr_prompts}
121|     response_data = _post_with_retry(api_address, pickle.dumps(payload))
122|     ocr_rewards = response_data["scores"]
123| 
124|     rewards = [None for _ in range(len(images))]
125|     for idx, reward in zip(ocr_idx, ocr_rewards):
126|         rewards[idx] = reward
127|     return rewards
128| 
129| 
130| def _safe_extract_score(text, default=0.0, min_val=1.0, max_val=5.0):
131|     """Extract a score from a possibly-noisy model output line."""
132|     import re
133| 
134|     try:
135|         score = float(text.strip())
136|     except (ValueError, AttributeError):
137|         try:
138|             match = re.search(r"(\d+\.?\d*)", str(text))
139|             if match:
140|                 score = float(match.group(1))
141|             else:
142|                 return default
143|         except (ValueError, AttributeError):
144|             return default
145|     if score < min_val or score > max_val:
146|         score = max(min_val, min(max_val, score))
147|     return score
148| 
149| 
150| def unified_reward(images, **kwargs):
151|     """Unified VLM-judge reward via vLLM. Alignment + coherence + style on 1–5 scale,
152|     combined via weights (0.4 / 0.4 / 0.2) and normalized to [0, 1]."""
153|     api_address = kwargs.get("api_address", os.environ.get("UNIFIED_REWARD_API_ADDRESS"))
154|     raw_prompts = kwargs.get("raw_prompt")
155| 
156|     batch_data = []
157|     for raw_prompt, image in zip(raw_prompts, images):
158|         problem = (
159|             "You are presented with a generated image and its associated text caption. "
160|             "Your task is to analyze the image across multiple dimensions in relation to the caption. Specifically:\n"
161|             "Provide overall assessments for the image along the following axes (each rated from 1 to 5):\n"
162|             "- Alignment Score: How well the image matches the caption in terms of content.\n"
163|             "- Coherence Score: How logically consistent the image is (absence of visual glitches, object distortions, etc.).\n"
164|             "- Style Score: How aesthetically appealing the image looks, regardless of caption accuracy.\n\n"
165|             "Output your evaluation using the format below:\n\n"
166|             "Alignment Score (1-5): X\n"
167|             "Coherence Score (1-5): Y\n"
168|             "Style Score (1-5): Z\n\n"
169|             "Your task is provided as follows:\n"
170|             f"Text Caption: [{raw_prompt}]"
171|         )
172|         batch_data.append({"problem": problem, "images": [image]})
173| 
174|     results = evaluate_batch(batch_data, api_address, image_root=None, server_name="UnifiedReward")
175| 
176|     rewards = []
177|     for result in results:
178|         output = result["model_output"]
179|         alignment_score = coherence_score = style_score = 0.0
180|         try:
181|             for line in output.split("\n"):
182|                 if "Alignment Score" in line:
183|                     score_text = line.split(":", 1)[1] if ":" in line else ""
184|                     alignment_score = _safe_extract_score(score_text, default=0.0)
185|                 elif "Coherence Score" in line:
186|                     score_text = line.split(":", 1)[1] if ":" in line else ""
187|                     coherence_score = _safe_extract_score(score_text, default=0.0)
188|                 elif "Style Score" in line:
189|                     score_text = line.split(":", 1)[1] if ":" in line else ""
190|                     style_score = _safe_extract_score(score_text, default=0.0)
191|         except Exception as e:
192|             logger.warning(f"[unified_reward] failed to parse model output: {e}")
193| 
194|         reward = (alignment_score * 0.4 + coherence_score * 0.4 + style_score * 0.2) / 5.0
195|         rewards.append(reward)
196|     return rewards

1| # RL Training (GRPO)
2| 
3| UniAR uses **GRPO** (Group Relative Policy Optimization) with a multi-reward stack to improve image generation quality via reinforcement learning.
4| 
5| ## Architecture
6| 
7| The RL training system consists of three types of nodes that communicate via HTTP and a shared filesystem:
8| 
9| ```
10| ┌─── Decode Node ──────────┐   ┌─── Reward Node ──────────────────┐
11| │  decode server           │   │  hpsv2                           │
12| │  (BSQ visual codes → PNG)│   │  geneval                         │
13| └──────────┬───────────────┘   │  ocr                             │
14|            │                   │  unified_reward                  │
15|            │                   └──────────┬───────────────────────┘
16|            │  HTTP                        │  HTTP
17|            ▼                              ▼
18| ┌─── Training Node(s) ────────────────────────────────────────────┐
19| │  train_grpo.py → UniARGRPOTrainer                               │
20| │    1. AR rollout → BSQ visual codes                             │
21| │    2. Send codes to decode server → PNG                         │
22| │    3. Send PNG to reward servers → scores                       │
23| │    4. GRPO loss update                                          │
24| └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
25|            │
26|            ▼
27|     SHARED_DIR (shared filesystem)
28|     ├── decoder_config.json     # decode server URLs
29|     ├── decoder_ready.flag
30|     ├── unified_reward_config.json
31|     ├── unified_reward_ready.flag
32|     ├── ...
33| ```
34| 
35| All nodes discover each other via **flag files** in a shared directory (`SHARED_DIR`). Training nodes wait for all services to be ready before starting. A typical deployment uses 3–4 nodes: 1 decode + 1 reward + 1–2 training (8 GPUs each).
36| 
37| ---
38| 
39| ## Quick Start (Single-Node)
40| 
41| For a minimal test on a single machine, use `run_reward_server.sh` to start servers individually:
42| 
43| ```bash
44| conda activate uniar
45| 
46| # Terminal 1: decode server (uses UniAR decoder weights)
47| SD3_TRANSFORMER_PATH=/path/to/sd3_transformer \
48| SD3_PATH=/path/to/sd3_pipeline \
49| IMAGE_TOKENIZER_PATH=/path/to/bsq_encoder \
50| bash scripts/train/run_reward_server.sh decode
51| 
52| # Terminal 2: hpsv2 reward
53| HPSV2_CKPT=/path/to/HPS_v2.1_compressed.pt \
54| CLIP_PATH=/path/to/CLIP-ViT-H-14 \
55| bash scripts/train/run_reward_server.sh hpsv2
56| 
57| # Terminal 3: training (minimal config)
58| MODEL_PATH=/path/to/ar_model \
59| DATA_PATH=data/rl_s1/s1_mix.yaml \
60| MASTER_ADDR=localhost \
61| SHARED_DIR=/tmp/uniar_rl \
62| REWARD_WEIGHTS="[1.0]" \
63| REWARD_FUNCTION_NAMES="[hpsv2_reward]" \
64| WAIT_SERVICES="decoder" \
65| MAX_STEPS=10 \
66| bash scripts/train/run_train_node.sh
67| ```
68| 
69| ---
70| 
71| ## Multi-Node Setup
72| 
73| For production training, run each service type on a dedicated node.
74| 
75| ### Step 1: Start decode servers
76| 
77| ```bash
78| # On the decode node
79| SHARED_DIR=/shared/run01 \
80| SD3_TRANSFORMER_PATH=/path/to/sd3_transformer \
81| SD3_PATH=/path/to/sd3_pipeline \
82| IMAGE_TOKENIZER_PATH=/path/to/bsq_encoder \
83| DECODE_NUM_GPUS=8 \
84| bash scripts/train/run_decode_node.sh
85| ```
86| 
87| ### Step 2: Start reward servers
88| 
89| ```bash
90| # On the reward node (launches selected rewards)
91| SHARED_DIR=/shared/run01 \
92| UNIFIED_REWARD_MODEL=CodeGoat24/UnifiedReward-2.0-qwen3vl-32b \
93| GENEVAL_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/mask2former.py \
94| GENEVAL_CKPT_PATH=/path/to/mask2former_weights \
95| HPSV2_CKPT=/path/to/HPS_v2.1_compressed.pt \
96| CLIP_PATH=/path/to/CLIP-ViT-H-14 \
97| bash scripts/train/run_reward_node.sh unified_reward geneval hpsv2 ocr
98| ```
99| 
100| ### Step 3: Launch training
101| 
102| ```bash
103| # On each training node
104| SHARED_DIR=/shared/run01 \
105| MODEL_PATH=/path/to/ar_model \
106| DATA_PATH=data/rl_s1/s1_mix.yaml \
107| MASTER_ADDR=<training_node_0_ip> \
108| NODE_RANK=0 \
109| bash scripts/train/run_train_node.sh
110| ```
111| 
112| For multi-node training, run the same command on each node with a different `NODE_RANK`.
113| 
114| ---
115| 
116| ## Training Data Format
117| 
118| Each JSONL record:
119| 
120| ```json
121| {
122|   "instruction": "A photo of a cat sitting on a windowsill",
123|   "number": 12345,
124|   "task": "geneval",
125|   "metadata": {"tag": "single_object", "include": ["cat"]}
126| }
127| ```
128| 
129| | Field | Required | Description |
130| |-------|----------|-------------|
131| | `instruction` | Yes | Text prompt for image generation |
132| | `number` | Yes | Unique integer ID (used for logging) |
133| | `task` | No | Specifies which reward functions to apply. Supported values: `geneval`, `ocr`, or omitted/`null` (general-purpose rewards only). See [`train/rl/reward_funcs.py`](../train/rl/reward_funcs.py) for the reward routing logic |
134| | `metadata` | No | Reward-specific metadata (e.g. GenEval `tag`/`include`/`exclude`) |
135| 
136| > **Note on OCR prompts:** For `task: "ocr"`, the target text to be rendered must be enclosed in double quotes within the instruction. The OCR reward function extracts quoted text as the ground truth for evaluation. Example: `"A store sign that reads \"Open 24 Hours\" in bold neon letters"`.
137| 
138| **YAML mix config** — sample from multiple JSONL files:
139| 
140| ```yaml
141| datasets:
142|   - name: blip3o_60k
143|     json_path: data/rl_s1/blip3o_60k.jsonl
144|     sampled_ratio: 10000       # integer: exact count
145|   - name: geneval_raw
146|     json_path: data/rl_s1/geneval_raw.jsonl
147|     sampled_ratio: 10000
148| ```
149| 
150| `sampled_ratio`: integer = exact sample count; float in (0,1) = fraction.
151| 
152| ---
153| 
154| ## Key Training Parameters
155| 
156| Set via environment variables before calling `run_train_node.sh`:
157| 
158| | Variable | Default | Description |
159| |----------|---------|-------------|
160| | `MODEL_PATH` | *(required)* | AR model checkpoint |
161| | `DATA_PATH` | *(required)* | Training data (JSONL or YAML) |
162| | `MASTER_ADDR` | *(required)* | IP of training node 0 |
163| | `SHARED_DIR` | *(required)* | Shared filesystem for service discovery |
164| | `NNODES` | 2 | Number of training nodes |
165| | `NODE_RANK` | 0 | This node's rank |
166| | `NPROC_PER_NODE` | 8 | GPUs per node |
167| | `LR` | 5e-6 | Learning rate |
168| | `BETA` | 0.01 | GRPO KL penalty coefficient |
169| | `LOSS_TYPE` | grpo | Loss type (`grpo` or `dapo`) |
170| | `TEMPERATURE` | 1.0 | Sampling temperature for rollouts |
171| | `NUM_GENERATIONS` | 16 | GRPO group size |
172| | `PER_DEVICE_BS` | 2 | Per-device batch size |
173| | `GRAD_ACC` | 16 | Gradient accumulation steps |
174| | `MAX_STEPS` | 500 | Maximum training steps |
175| | `SAVE_STEPS` | 50 | Checkpoint save interval |
176| | `REWARD_WEIGHTS` | `[1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]` | Per-reward weights |
177| | `REWARD_FUNCTION_NAMES` | `[unified_reward, geneval_reward, ocr_reward, hpsv2_reward]` | Active reward functions |
178| | `WAIT_SERVICES` | `decoder unified_reward ocr` | Services to wait for before starting |
179| 
180| ---
181| 
182| ## Reward Servers
183| 
184| | Server | Conda env | GPU | Key weights |
185| |--------|-----------|-----|-------------|
186| | **decode** | `uniar` (same as training) | 1+ GPU | SD3 transformer + pipeline + BSQ encoder |
187| | **hpsv2** | `hpsv2` | CPU/GPU | HPSv2 + CLIP-ViT-H-14 |
188| | **geneval** | `geneval` (Python 3.9) | GPU | Mask2Former (mmdet 2.x) |
189| | **ocr** | `ocr` | CPU | PaddleOCR (auto-downloaded) |
190| | **unified_reward** | `unified_reward` | 4+ GPU | UnifiedReward-2.0-qwen3vl-32b via vLLM |
191| 
192| See [docs/reward_servers.md](reward_servers.md) for detailed environment setup, weight downloads, and launch commands for each server.
193| 
194| ---
195| 
196| ## Scripts Reference
197| 
198| | Script | Purpose |
199| |--------|---------|
200| | `scripts/train/run_train_node.sh` | Launch training on one node |
201| | `scripts/train/run_decode_node.sh` | Start decode servers + register in SHARED_DIR |
202| | `scripts/train/run_reward_node.sh` | Start multiple reward servers + register in SHARED_DIR |
203| | `scripts/train/run_reward_server.sh` | Start a single reward server (standalone) |

(End of file — 203 lines total)
